en.title: Change Elements to Positive Integers So All k-Windows Have Equal Sums
en.description:
Any element may be changed to a positive integer, and each changed position counts once. Every contiguous subarray of length k must have the same sum; find the minimum number of changes. Original elements may be non-positive; unchanged positions do not need to become positive. When k≥n, no change is needed.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k; the second line contains the integer array. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n,k≤200000, −10^9≤element≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 1, 0 and 2. In the last example 2 cannot be changed to −1; the only option is to change the two −1s to 2.
hints: Subtracting adjacent windows gives a[i]=a[i+k]. Group the indices by index mod k: a group whose values are already all equal stays unchanged; otherwise set the group to its most frequent positive value, or change everything to 1 if it has no positive value.
